content: The combination of abacavir, dolutegravir, and lamivudine is indicated for the treatment of HIV-1 infection. The standard dosage is one tablet (600 mg/50 mg/300 mg) taken orally once daily. If co-administered with efavirenz, fosamprenavir/ritonavir, tipranavir/ritonavir, carbamazepine, or rifampin, an additional 50 mg dolutegravir tablet (as a single entity) should be taken 12 hours apart from the abacavir/dolutegravir/lamivudine dose. This combination is not recommended for patients with a current or past history of resistance to any of its components. For children aged 3 months and weighing at least 6 kg, this combination is also indicated for HIV-1 treatment. However, its safety and efficacy have not been established in children weighing less than 6 kg. Triumeq and Triumeq PD should not be interchanged on a milligram-per-milligram basis. Triumeq PD is recommended for children weighing 6 to less than 25 kg, while Triumeq is for those weighing at least 25 kg. The combination of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be administered with other antiretrovirals. Co-administration of emtricitabine-containing products and lamivudine-containing products should be avoided due to the risk of therapeutic duplication and increased risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Similarly, lamivudine should not be co-administered with atidarsagene autotemcel, betibeglogene autotemcel, or lovotibeglogene autotemcel, as antiretroviral medications may interfere with the manufacturing of these cell-based therapies. Antiretroviral therapy (ART) should be discontinued at least one month before cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Tafenoquine, an inhibitor of organic cation transporter-2 (OCT2) and multidrug and toxin extrusion (MATE) transporters, increases lamivudine levels. Co-administration with OCT2 or MATE substrates should be avoided, or substrate-related toxicities should be monitored closely. Lamivudine increases the levels of cabozantinib by inhibiting MRP2 transporters, which may increase cabozantinib toxicity. Similarly, lamivudine increases the levels of erdafitinib by decreasing renal clearance. Alternatives to OCT2 substrates or dose adjustments should be considered. Co-administration of lamivudine with trimethoprim may increase lamivudine effects due to competition for renal tubular clearance, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Lamivudine and other antiretrovirals, such as abacavir, atazanavir, efavirenz, enfuvirtide, fosamprenavir, indinavir, nelfinavir, nevirapine, ritonavir, tenofovir DF, and tipranavir, all increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Close monitoring is recommended in these cases. Co-administration of lamivudine with interferon alfa-2b or peginterferon alfa-2a/2b increases the risk of liver decompensation. Ribavirin increases the risk of lactic acidosis when combined with lamivudine, and caution is advised. Lamivudine and zidovudine exhibit beneficial pharmacodynamic synergy, but both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Co-administration of lamivudine with valganciclovir or ganciclovir increases the risk of hematologic toxicity. Ublituximab decreases the effects of lamivudine due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Abacavir, dolutegravir, and lamivudine are present in human milk, but it is unknown whether they affect milk production or the breastfed infant. Breastfeeding carries potential risks, including HIV-1 transmission to HIV-negative infants, development of viral resistance in HIV-positive infants, and adverse reactions in the breastfed infant similar to those seen in adults. Abacavir is a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) that inhibits HIV-1 reverse transcriptase by competing with dGTP, thereby inhibiting viral replication. Dolutegravir is an integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI) that inhibits the catalytic activity of HIV-1 integrase, an enzyme required for viral replication. Lamivudine, also an NRTI, inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase following phosphorylation, leading to viral DNA chain termination. Abacavir is primarily metabolized by alcohol dehydrogenase and glucuronyl transferase. Dolutegravir is metabolized via UGT1A1 with some contribution from CYP3A. Lamivudine metabolism is negligible. Patients carrying the HLA-B5701 allele are at high risk for hypersensitivity reactions to abacavir. Screening for this allele is required before initiating abacavir therapy, and treatment with abacavir-containing regimens is contraindicated in HLA-B5701-positive patients. The combination can be taken with or without food. Tablets should not be chewed, cut, or crushed. Triumeq and Triumeq PD should not be interchanged on a milligram-per-milligram basis. The medication should be stored at room temperature (20–25°C or 68–77°F) in its original packaging, protected from moisture, and with the bottle tightly closed. The desiccant should not be removed.
